title: Effects of Infill Patterns on Mechanical Properties of Chopped Carbon Fiber Reinforced Composites Produced by Fused Deposition Modeling
content: A composite is a material composed of two or more substances with distinct chemical and physical properties. Components consist of two parts: a fiber and a matrix. The fibers can be materials like polyethylene, glass, carbon fiber (CF), or Kevlar, while the matrix holds the fibers in place. The matrix is typically a thermoset, such as epoxy resin or polyimide [1]. To enhance the strength of the matrix, the fibers are embedded within it. This structure forms one of the most common types of composite materials, known as fiber-reinforced composites [2]. Today, polymer composites are used in a wide range of industries. Their unique physical, chemical, and mechanical properties distinguish them from other metals. Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) is an additive manufacturing (AM) technique that directly creates parts with intricate geometries in their final form, without the need for extra specialized tools or equipment. This process constructs parts by depositing material layer by layer precisely where required, reducing energy consumption, costs, production time for complex components, and minimizing waste [3]. In this report, we present various infill print patterns of FDM printed Markforged onyx filament samples with chopped up CF reinforcement. The effects of infill print patterns of the FDM samples in relation to microstructure, CF arrangement and mechanical properties were characterized.
